A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same SeeU research. Their main text, equations, tables, figures, and complete supplementary materials are readable and support reliable comparison, including matching relocated and renumbered content.

before.justification: Tables 1-3 report original temporal and spatial generation experiments on SeeU45 and ablations of architecture, physics loss, and input sparsity.

after.justification: The original experiments are retained, with additional qualitative robustness evaluations in Figure 10 and numerical comparisons in Table 5.

M1.justification: The reconstruction, B-spline dynamics modeling, losses, and context-conditioned generation pipeline remain unchanged, as does Algorithm 1. Processing longer videos in stable chunks is suggested in v2, not reported as an implemented procedure.

E1.justification: SeeU45 and the temporal generation, spatial generation, and editing tasks are retained. Figure 10 adds explicit challenging scenarios involving crowds, interactions, chaotic motion, degraded inputs, longer sequences, and partial visibility. These are not identified as a new dataset.

E2.justification: New Table 5 evaluates DaS and HunyuanWorld-Voyager against SeeU. Both comparators are absent from v1's experiments; the existing main-text comparator sets remain unchanged.

E3.justification: New Figure 10 includes additional camera-control settings, notably tilt-down and pan-left. Existing splits, training budgets, metrics, and 6.67% past/future evaluation windows remain unchanged. Table 5 does not specify its scene selection or aggregation protocol.

E4.justification: Section 13 and Figure 10 introduce a broad qualitative robustness examination across eight challenging examples, probing combinations of adverse motion, interactions, input quality, visibility, and sequence length. This substantially extends the analysis beyond v1's component ablations, input-sparsity study, and limited failure examples, which are retained.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, random seeds, confidence intervals, significance tests, or comparable uncertainty estimates. The new evaluations introduce no statistical reporting procedure.

E6.justification: Existing numerical tables and plots are unchanged. Table 5 newly reports EIR/CLIP-V of 0.8024/0.9588 for SeeU, 0.7624/0.9253 for DaS, and 0.7298/0.8911 for HunyuanWorld-Voyager; Figure 10 adds qualitative outcomes. These are additional results, not demonstrated same-setting improvements over v1.

T1.justification: Equations 1-11, the mathematical dynamics formulation, and the geometric metric definitions are unchanged. No new formal assumptions, derivations, theorems, or proofs are introduced.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction's contribution statements, and conclusion retain the same claims about the 2D-to-4D-to-2D framework, continuous dynamics, and temporal, spatial, and editing applications.

C2.justification: Section 13 discusses applicability to challenging inputs while acknowledging residual artifacts and suggests stable temporal chunks for longer videos. Section 14 attributes differentiation from the new comparators to temporal dynamics modeling. Existing upstream-geometry and foreground-detail limitations remain unchanged.

D1.justification: The final visual-results section changes its video-access instruction from the project page to supplementary materials. Implementation details, hyperparameters, hardware, training times, dataset construction, and the code/data release statement remain unchanged. The PDFs do not establish actual availability of additional video files.

R1.justification: Five cited works are added, including Diffusion as Shader and Voyager. Section 14 explicitly positions SeeU against their 3D/4D memory-based designs. The broader related-work organization is retained; DELTAv2's changed title refers to the same cited work.

P1.justification: v2 corrects spelling in the Section 4.3 heading, updates the supplementary roadmap, and inserts robustness and comparison sections before the retained visual-results section. The main scientific prose is otherwise essentially unchanged.

P2.justification: v2 adds Figure 10 and Table 5, relocates and resizes Figure 3, and enlarges labels and increases image resolution in the retained supplementary visual examples. Former Figures 10-12 become Figures 11-13; their examples are preserved.

improvement.justification: The added comparisons with related 3D/4D methods and challenging-case examples improve empirical context and applicability assessment while preserving the original evidence. The gain is limited: Table 5 lacks evaluation setup details, robustness evidence is qualitative, and the proposed chunking strategy is untested. These additions do not establish that the original limitations are resolved.
